title: Which files are plugins?
description:
The host scans its plugin folder. For each file it gathers what it found, and must decide which plugins to keep. Write

```cpp
struct Candidate
{
    std::string file;              // file name, e.g. "fog.dll"
    bool loads{ true };            // LoadLibraryExW succeeded
    bool hasExport{ true };        // GetProcAddress found xenon_get_plugin
    uint32_t tableSize{ 0 };       // plugin->size
    uint32_t apiVersion{ 0 };      // plugin->api_version
    std::string name;              // plugin->name
    bool startOk{ true };          // plugin->start returned 0
};

struct ScanResult { std::vector<std::string> kept; std::vector<std::string> log; };

ScanResult scanPlugins(const std::vector<Candidate>& files, uint32_t hostApiVersion, uint32_t requiredTableSize);
```

Go through the files **sorted by file name** (case-insensitive) and apply the checks in this order. The first one that fails adds a line to `log` and skips the file:

1. The name must end in `.dll` (any case), otherwise: `"<file>: not a DLL"`.
2. `loads`, otherwise: `"<file>: could not load"`.
3. `hasExport`, otherwise: `"<file>: not a plugin"`.
4. `tableSize >= requiredTableSize` and `apiVersion == hostApiVersion`, otherwise: `"<file>: built for API version <apiVersion>, need <hostApiVersion>"`.
5. A plugin `name` that has not been kept already (exact comparison), otherwise: `"<file>: duplicate plugin <name>"`.
6. `startOk`, otherwise: `"<file>: start failed"`.

A file that passes everything adds its plugin `name` to `kept` and the log line `"<file>: loaded <name>"`.
